html:
SMTO-SKL-0106 — SMTO can't access that SharePoint site

GUID: 5fd0da91-b04a-590d-bd27-61ee43e9bc5b
Slug: microsoft365-site-not-authorized
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: microsoft365

What happened

  • Either your Microsoft account doesn't have permission for this SharePoint site, or the document library chosen doesn't belong to that site. SMTO stopped before doing anything there.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the SharePoint site in your web browser with the same Microsoft account and check you can see its documents. SMTO can only reach sites your own account has permission to use.
  2. Ask the Agent to list the document libraries for that site, then pick one from that list. A library from a different site can't be used with this site.
  3. If you can open the site but SMTO still can't, ask the Agent to reconnect your Microsoft 365 account with SharePoint access added. SharePoint needs its own permission, separate from OneDrive.

What success looks like

  • The Agent lists the site's files or completes your request.

If it still fails

  • Ask the site owner or your Microsoft administrator to give your account access, or to approve SharePoint access for SMTO. Then select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO if it still fails.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • SharePoint access is denied or the selected drive belongs to a different site.

What this means

  • Graph denies a SharePoint-scoped request, or the supplied drive's SharePoint site identity does not match the selected site. This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Graph denies a SharePoint-scoped request, or the supplied drive's SharePoint site identity does not match the selected site.

How to diagnose it

  • Distinguish provider denial from an explicit drive/site identity mismatch.

How to fix it

  • Confirm the signed-in user can open the site in SharePoint and that drive_id belongs to site_id (the drive's sharepointIds.siteId must match the site's). If Graph returned 403, reconnect with only the needed sharepoint_read or sharepoint_write feature; tenant policy may require administrator consent for Sites.Read.All/Sites.ReadWrite.All.
  • Verify the exact site/drive relationship and selected user's access; request only the required explicit SharePoint feature.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect provider state and exact account authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • An authorized drive and site match the intended scope and required feature.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
